extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A subset of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater. The tasks include traditional NLP, mathematics, commonsense reasoning, and question-answering, requiring multi-step reasoning capabilities.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: BIG-Bench Hard was curated by filtering BIG-Bench tasks based on specific criteria including task size, human-rater baselines, evaluation metrics, and model performance relative to human-raters.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For all but three tasks in BBH, a random subset of 250 evaluation examples was taken. For Causal Judgement, Penguins in a Table, and Snarks, all available test examples were considered in addition to three examples reserved for few-shot prompting.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tasks were filtered based on multiple criteria: tasks with more than three subtasks were excluded, tasks with fewer than 103 examples were excluded, tasks without human-rater baselines were excluded, tasks not using multiple-choice or exact match evaluation were excluded, tasks where best model beat average human-rater were excluded, and extremely difficult tasks outside the scope were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Chain-of-thought exemplars were manually composed for each task. Three chain-of-thought exemplars were created per task, with 'let's think step-by-step' prepended to all CoT annotations in the few-shot exemplars.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper notes that certain tasks were excluded from BBH due to concerns about delegating moral judgement scenarios to models, specifically mentioning the Moral Permissibility task.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The human-rater performance scores are not fully representative of the entire population and should be interpreted with care. Human-raters were allocated a few hours per day to solve tasks and could use external resources. Some task descriptions were hard to follow and could have been better-formulated. Surpassing average human-rater performance should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating language model capabilities on challenging tasks requiring multi-step reasoning, particularly for testing chain-of-thought prompting approaches. The benchmark contains 6,511 evaluation examples across 23 tasks.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: In this paper, we curate BIG-Bench Hard (BBH), a subset of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks (27 subtasks) for which no prior result from Srivastava et al. (2022) has outperformed the average human-rater score.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: BIG-Bench is a collaborative benchmark that aims to quantitatively measure the capabilities and limitations of language models (Srivastava et al., 2022, Beyond the Imitation Game Benchmark). The benchmark has over 200 diverse text-based tasks

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For all but three tasks in BBH, we take a random subset of 250 evaluation examples. For Causal Judgement, Penguins in a Table, and Snarks, we consider all the available test examples—namely, 187, 146, and 178, respectively—in addition to the three examples reserved for few-shot prompting.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We, therefore, choose a set of criteria (listed in Table 1) to filter BIG-Bench to arrive at a clean, challenging, and tractable subset... These filtering criteria result in 78 clean multiple-choice or exact-match tasks.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We manually compose three chain-of-thought exemplars for each task in BBH; all the prompts used are shown in Section C. We prepend 'let's think step-by-step' (Kojima et al., 2022) to all CoT annotations in the few-shot exemplars.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Moral Permissibility has an ambiguous task formulation (and we did not want to delegate agency to models about moral judgement scenarios (Talat et al., 2022)).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We note that even though Srivastava et al. (2022) report the average and maximum of human-rater performances on most BIG-Bench tasks; the organizers acknowledge that one should be careful in interpreting these results because the scores are not fully representative of human performance... Therefore, surpassing average human-rater performance score on a set of challenging tasks should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In this work, we focus on a suite of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks which we call BIG-Bench Hard (BBH). These are the task for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater... Hence, there are 6,511 evaluation examples in the benchmark in total.
